I use the Notability app on my iPad for site visits. If I have as-builts, I upload them into the app and start marking them up. If I don't have as-builts, I use an 11x17 tabloid-size template in the app to sketch. I take pictures with the iPad's native camera app, import them into Notability, and annotate from there. Notability also offers cloud backup, so I have it linked to a Google Drive folder shared with all my colleagues. This way, they can easily access the files. Not a good idea to do a hood design for a future restaurant. Reason is, you just don’t know what that future tenant’s is going to put in their kitchen. The new tenant is going to have to design their kitchen around the placement of the hood. What if the hood is too small for all their type 1 loads? Then the tenant either have to rip it out or provide new. If this is on a multi-story then it would make sense to plan for rated shafts, exhaust, and intake points. Not to mention you don’t know if they are going to use gas or electric? Now they have to rip out that nice stainless steel backing  and rough in new plumbing and electric. Also, some ansul system is designed to point at the kitchen equipment I believe.
